title: Malformed pairs are rejected
statement: Let $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $V$ be a language of finite bit strings, and let $y$ be a finite bit string. If the aligned pair parser is undefined on $y$, then $y$ does not belong to the paired verifier language defined by $C,c,$ and $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of finite bit strings
The aligned pair parser returns no pair on $y$
replaced:
Let $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$ and $V \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$. The aligned pair parser
reads a binary string in two-bit blocks from the left, taking $00$ and $11$ as the
bits $0$ and $1$ of a first component until the first block $01$, after which the
remaining suffix is the second component; it fails on every other string. Let
$V^{\mathrm{pair}}_{C,c}$ be the set of strings that this parser decodes as a pair
$(x, u)$ with $|u| = C(|x|+1)^c$ and $xu \in V$. If $y$ is a binary string on
which the parser fails, then $y \notin V^{\mathrm{pair}}_{C,c}$.
